raw_affiliation_strings: Assistant Professor of Anthropology and Jewish Studies at Pennsylvania State University (University Park, Pa. 16802–3404, U.S.A.). He has been a senior staff member of the Megiddo excavation and survey project in Israel and has participated in fieldwork in Jordan, Greece, and the United States. His research interests are archaeological theory, the evolution of complex societies, and the intellectual and social history of archaeology. His publications include Settlement and Society in the Early Bronze I and II Southern Levant: Complementarity and Contradiction in a Small‐Scale Complex Society (Sheffield: Sheffield Academic Press, 1993) and “‘Disembedded Capitals’ in Western Asian Perspective” (Comparative Studies in Society and History, in press). The present paper was submitted 7 Iv 97 and accepted 26 VIII 97; the final version reached the Editor's office 26 IX 97
